analysis:
Examined the SSD prefix cache changes. SSDPrefixCache.swift (units 8 and 9) shows only a comment edit near line 1081, which describes the new write-charging order. The staging, read, validation and removal logic in the supplied excerpt is unchanged and was reviewed as context. It still enforces epoch checks, AES-GCM authenticated reads with metadata binding to weightHash, layoutEpoch, blockSize and lookupTag, and safe-root/no-symlink checks. Corrupt files are deleted and de-indexed. The HMAC lookup-tag, TTL, KEK and account-scoping mitigations in T-041 are untouched.

SSDWriteBehind.swift (base lines 296-301, head patch hunks) changes the endurance accounting. When a job has more than one block, chargeWholeDonation sums serializedByteCount for all blocks with overflow checking and makes a single rateLimiter.tryConsume. If that charge succeeds, the per-block tryConsume is skipped (prepaid). If the sum fails, overflows or is refused, nothing is charged and the per-block path runs as before, which is fail-safe.

Security-relevant observations:
- Total charged bytes equal the sum of the per-block charges, so the daily write-endurance cap is not weakened.
- Blocks skipped after a successful prepay (cancellation, unsafe URL, write failure) stay charged. That is conservative, so it cannot cause over-writing.
- The low-disk floor check and the ENOSPC cooldown are unchanged and run before the charge.
- The prepay is not rolled back on a later partial failure. That only reduces availability marginally and is documented in the code.
- A single-block job is never prepaid, so the behaviour is unchanged for that case.

No new at-rest artifacts, key handling, trust boundary or authorization surface were introduced. Remaining unverified: the SSDWriteRateLimiter implementation (tryConsume semantics and durable ledger) is outside the supplied evidence. The patch excerpt of SSDWriteBehind is marked incomplete, but the base text and visible hunks cover the changed ranges. No threat-model update appears necessary.
